messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: micro_era5 and micro_ncep change
parts:
Hi everyone,
I wanted to alert you to a change I've made to micro_era5 and micro_ncep to prevent them from getting stuck in endless loops in some circumstances. The short story is it won't make any difference to your calculations other than preventing the endless loops.

The longer story is that I found that in some places the integrator was having difficulty finding a solution on days with a relatively large daily precipitation. In the microclimate model, the precipitation meant to fall daily at midnight. However, because the input data for micro_ncep and micro_era5 can start at times other than midnight, depending on the timezone (because it is based on UTC), there were situations where the precipitation was falling when there was high solar radiation. I've fixed it by putting the daily rainfall into the hourly rainfall input vector, on the hours that are local solar midnight.

Hope that makes sense. The change is presently only on the github version.

All the best,
Mike

Hi Mike,

I have some questions about the rainhourly vector that you can input in the microclimate model (using micro_ncep function).
I am running the micro_ncep function on repeated locations but it seems that depending on the coordinates, for same dates and rainfall input, the snowdepth is not always well modelled (production of NaN in the metout output).

If the 'rainhour' vector is provided (with rainhourly = 1) and is only a vector of hourly rainfall values, how does the model knows exactly at which dates the vector is starting and ending?
Did you test this parameter running micro_ncep function on multiple years and modelling snowfalls and snowdepths?

I also tried inputing daily rainfall values (with dailyprecip), which works well on the different coordinates.

I don't know if someone else has tried the rainhour parameter and managed to get it work?
I am using the 3.2.1 NicheMapR version.

Thank you very much!

And then I check the metout object (with TALOC and SNOWDEP).

Sorry to take a while with this - it does seem that the integrator is having trouble with the sudden jumps in rainfall. I've just pushed a change to micro_ncep and micro_era5 so that when you pass hourly rainfall to the model but set rainhourly=0, it will aggregate the hourly rainfall to daily and make it fall at midnight. Can you give this new version a try in this way and see if it works? I haven't had a chance to test it myself.

All the best,
Mike

Hi everyone,
I wanted to alert you to a change I've made to micro_era5 and micro_ncep to prevent them from getting stuck in endless loops in some circumstances. The short story is it won't make any difference to your calculations other than preventing the endless loops.

The longer story is that I found that in some places the integrator was having difficulty finding a solution on days with a relatively large daily precipitation. In the microclimate model, the precipitation meant to fall daily at midnight. However, because the input data for micro_ncep and micro_era5 can start at times other than midnight, depending on the timezone (because it is based on UTC), there were situations where the precipitation was falling when there was high solar radiation. I've fixed it by putting the daily rainfall into the hourly rainfall input vector, on the hours that are local solar midnight.

Hope that makes sense. The change is presently only on the github version.

All the best,
Mike
